outcome: Say when a sort leaves the order of tied rows open (G27): a transform whose output order is set by a sort step that some rows tie on comes back with advice naming the tie, so the agent can add a key before a preview and a materialization order those rows differently
criteria: A successful transform_dataset or materialize_result whose output order is set by its last sort step (followed only by select, derive, rename and at most one limit) carries sort_ties advice when rows tie on that step's keys: how many rows tie, the key values of the largest tied group and its size, that their order is not determined between runs, and that a key telling them apart settles it

With a limit after the sort, only tied groups that reach into the rows the limit keeps are counted, and the advice says the limit can keep different rows; tied rows wholly outside the kept rows are silent

No advice when the sort keys separate every row, when no sort step sets the output order (none, or an aggregate or join after it), or when the transform starts with a raw_query; the tie count never fails a transform

Tests on data unrelated to any benchmark cover a tie, a tie at a limit boundary, a tie outside the kept rows, a separating second key, and a sort followed by an aggregate; the test suite passes; README's teach-on-refusal section lists the signal

dispositions.note: tests/test_recovery.py covers a tie (preview and materialize), a separating second key, a tie at a limit boundary, ties outside the kept rows, and sorts followed by an aggregate, a filter, or after a raw_query; the full suite passes except the same 8 FFmpeg tests that need libx264, absent from this host's FFmpeg; README and the transform tool description name the signal

note: SqlCompiler.compile_ties builds the transform's CTE chain up to the sort that sets the output order (the last sort, followed only by select, derive, rename and at most one limit) and counts groups with more than one row on its keys, restricted with a limit to key values among the rows the limit keeps; it returns the largest group's keys and size, the group count and the tied-row count. The executor runs it after any transform that returned rows and does not start with a raw_query, guarded so a failure only drops the count. advise_sort_ties explains without a rewrite: which column separates the rows is the agent's to choose. A sort followed by a filter is not counted, since the filter can remove tied rows.
